title: Simplify color anchors and atomic spacing for mobile action bars
creator: Ethan Cho
description:
Problem: Mobile action bars (bottom nav, contextual toolbars, and floating action areas) currently use a mixture of legacy token aliases and hard-coded values across product surfaces. This has resulted in inconsistent contrast, uneven tappable spacing, and fragmented shadow treatments on narrow viewports.

Goal: Define a minimal, accessible palette of color anchors and an "atomic spacing" subset tuned for mobile action bars, plus a simplified elevation ladder for compact surfaces. The deliverables are: 1) a token spec with 6 color anchors (accent/neutral/surface variants) tuned for 320-420px widths; 2) an atomic spacing scale (4/8/12/16) and mapped radii presets for action controls; 3) a compact elevation set (two low-contrast penumbra steps) and guidance for layered overlays; 4) Figma components and a migration plan for React components.

Scope notes: This is intentionally conservative — we are not renaming the global token namespace or touching desktop density tokens. Mobile action-bar tokens should be additive aliases that migrate components incrementally. Accessibility targets: WCAG AA text contrast for primary and secondary states, 44px minimum tappable areas, consistent 12px minimum spacing between grouped actions.

Out of scope: full palette rebakes, dataviz chart colors, and deep changes to typography scale outside button labels and compact captions.
comments: 2026-02-20 - Ethan Cho: Created initial ticket after spike with two product teams. Attached early token sketches and a short video of current mismatches on iOS/Android webviews.

2026-02-24 - Nora Patel: Ran contrast checks against existing palette — several secondary icons fall below AA on dark surfaces. Proposed accents: anchor-accent-400 and anchor-accent-700 as primary/hover states.
2026-02-26 - Design Review (Luca Moreno): Prefer a 3-step elevation for overlays but keep action bars to 2 steps to reduce perceived clutter. Suggested removing drop shadows from floating badges.
2026-03-01 - PM sync (Aisha Raman): Customer feedback from mobile app 2.4 flags inconsistent tap targets; prioritized this as P1 for mobile stability milestone.
2026-03-03 - Engineering feedback (Priya Desai): The React Button component accepts token aliases; we can add new aliases behind a feature flag and run a small canary targeting mobile builds.
2026-03-05 - Nora Patel: Finalized first pass tokens in Figma: color anchors and atomic spacing variables added. Next: write migration notes and open RFC for token aliases.
next_steps: 1) Publish token aliases and short migration guide in Confluence (owner: Nora). 2) Open PR to add aliases and feature flag in component library (owner: Priya). 3) Schedule cross-functional review with mobile product owners on 2026-03-10. 4) Ship canary and monitor console usage + accessibility regression dashboard.
notes: Trade-offs: Using additive aliases keeps risk low but increases temporary token surface. If adoption stalls after two sprints, we'll deprecate a small set of legacy tokens and consolidate.
